newsitem.title: NORWAY: Esso begins removal of North Sea Odin gas platform.
newsitem.headline: Esso begins removal of North Sea Odin gas platform.

text.p: Esso Norge AS has begun the 250 million crown removal of the North Sea Odin gas platform, the first independent structure to be decomissioned and removed from Norway's continental shelf, the company said on Thursday.
Odin, a four-legged steel jacket plus topside, was shut in on August 1, 1994 after producing 27.7 billion cubic metres of gas over a 10-year life time.

Esso spokesman Arvid Barheim said the 7,600 tonne topside structure was separated from the jacket on Monday and taken to Aker ASA's Stord yard between Bergen and Stavanger on the west coast of Norway.
Aker is working with Italy's Saipem to remove the structure. Saipem owns the giant S7000 vessel, the world's largest crane barge, which is being used to transport the disused platform.
Barheim said the 7,700 tonne jacket would be cut up and removed in January.
Earlier this year Elf Petroleum removed the Northeast Frigg structure, a subsea template and control tower tied back to the Frigg development.
